articles.title: Baste Duterte asks impeachment court to reset trial appearance
articles.summary: The Davao mayor was directed to appear before the court and produce relevant records, including contracts with Gencorp

blocks.text: BASTE DUTERTE. Davao City Mayor Sebastian 'Baste' Duterte presides a meeting in this file photo taken in December 2025.
Mayor Sebastian 'Baste' Duterte Facebook page
The Davao mayor was directed to appear before the court and produce relevant records, including contracts with Gencorp

items: Davao City Mayor Sebastian Duterte requested the Senate impeachment court to rest the date of his testimony at the impeachment trial of his sister, Vice President Sara Duterte, to gather necessary documents.
The court granted his request, allowing him to appear on September 29 or 30 instead of the originally scheduled date.
The impeachment trial involves the Davao City Hall's contracts with Gencorp Industries Inc., which has raised concerns about potential conflicts of interest related to Vice President Sara Duterte.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Davao City mayor Sebastian “Baste” Duterte has asked the Senate impeachment court to reset the date of his testimony in the impeachment trial of his older sister, Vice President Sara Duterte.

On Day 28 of the trial, on Monday, September 28, presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero said the court has received a letter from Duterte requesting to be allowed to “gather, organize, authenticate, and reproduce” the documents being subpoenaed by the court and to appear before the court on Tuesday, September 29, or Wednesday, September 30.

“The court was in receipt of a letter from Mayor Sebastian Duterte of the city of Davao dated today requesting that among others, that he be given time as he requires substantial time to gather, organize, authenticate, and reproduce the subpoenaed documents and asks that he be allowed to attend instead of today, tomorrow and on Wednesday,” Escudero.
“The presiding officer grants the request of mayor Duterte to appear tomorrow and Wednesday,” he said.

The Davao mayor was earlier subpoenaed to appear before the court from September 28 to September 30. He was also ordered to produce certified true copies of relevant official records in the custody of the Davao City government, including “all contracts and similar transaction records entered into from 2020 to the present with: Gencorp Industries Inc.; and any corporation or other entity that owns or operates a Jollibee branch or establishment.”

Gencorp was linked to the Vice President after it was found that she declared herself as a stockholder of the company in her 2022, 2023, and 2024 Statements of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALNs). However, her name did not appear as an incorporator or stockholder in Gencorp’s corporate records, according to Securities and Exchange Commission Director Gerardo del Rosario.

Rappler earlier reported that Gencorp secured P15.02 million in food and catering contracts from Davao City Hall and PhilHealth between 2022 and 2025, raising concerns about potential conflicts of interest. Mayor Duterte himself said that Gencopr cornered at least 19 contracts worth P33.26 million, and that that all these transactions followed government procurement laws.
He had also denied that Sara’s name or even the Duterte surname appeared in any of the company’s official documents submitted to the Davao City government.

The impeachment court initially directed the mayor to appear at the trial on Wednesday, September 23. However, it recalled the subpoena and reset his appearance in view of the oral arguments on the voting threshold. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Authorities to verify ex-cop Gracioso's claims vs Dutertes --SILG Jonvic Remulla
articles.summary: Authorities will verify the allegations made by dismissed police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. against the Dutertes before accepting them as fact, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said Monday.

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 12:47pm
Authorities will verify the allegations made by dismissed police officer Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. against the Dutertes before accepting them as fact, Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said Monday.
“Titignan natin 'yung veracity ng kanyang sinabi, kung dinala niya talaga o kung may nadala. Hindi naman puwedeng agad accepted as katotohanan kaagad,” Remulla said in an ambush interview.
(We'll look at the veracity of what he said, whether he actually brought it or if he brought something. It can't be accepted as truth right away.)
“We'll study him. He will undergo the rigorous procedures of investigation para ma-determine talaga kung totoo sinasabi niya,” he added.
(We'll study him. He will undergo the rigorous procedures of investigation to determine if what he's saying is true.)
Remulla said he will also study the background of Gracioso.
“Ang background niya is nasa akin ngayon. Pag-aaralan ko kung noteworthy, kung tama ang sinasabi niya,” he said.
(I have his background now. I will study it if it is noteworthy, if what he is saying is true.)
“Alam mo, 'yung mga ganito kasi, maraming gusto magliyab ng sitwasyon eh. But, we will take all of his statements with all seriousness para malaman natin kung ano ang katotohanan,” he added.
(You know, in cases like this, many people want to inflame the situation. But, we will take all of his statements with all seriousness so we can know what the truth is.)
The Philippine National Police (PNP) meanwhile on Monday confirmed that Gracioso had previously been assigned to the security detail of then-House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
The PNP also confirmed that Gracioso was dismissed from the service on September 11 this year.

Gracioso, who claimed to have served as a security officer for former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco, surfaced last week and alleged that he delivered suitcases containing cash to Vice President Sara Duterte, former President Rodrigo Duterte, and Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo "Pulong" Duterte on Velasco’s instructions.
On Saturday, VP Sara said she does not know Gracioso, and she did not receive any money from him.
"My lawyers are awaiting an official copy of the Gracioso affidavit from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) so they can begin working on the cases to be filed against him," she added.
"Once we are done dismantling the lies contained in his testimony, it will end up in the trash bin—just like the one from Ramil Madriaga," she added.
Velasco’s camp on Saturday said the allegations against him had “no basis.”

"The former Speaker of the House's record of service in the government is untainted with corruption and his wife's benevolence is widely known, leaving no basis for the illegal allegations now being suggested," said Velasco's spokesperson Atty. Rowell Ilagan in a statement.

"The 'one-size-fits-all' narration by this individual seems to be designed and fabricated to attack as many targets as it can while being inconsistent with verifiable events, that is, the COVID-19 pandemic, Atty. Velasco's period of service as speaker, other details, and even basic common sense," he added.
Former chief presidential legal counsel Salvador Panelo said on Sunday that Gracioso’s claims are a “fabricated story” to oust and disqualify Vice President Sara Duterte in the 2028 elections.
“The Gracioso concoction is obviously another fabricated story, pure and simple black propaganda, just like the Madriaga affidavit,” Panelo said in a statement.

“The brains behind the ouster and disqualification of VP Sara in the 2028 presidential elections will stop at nothing in order to succeed in their devious plan of obliterating her from the political landscape and from the face of the earth,” he added. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Baste Duterte seeks more time to prepare for Sara impeachment trial appearance
articles.summary: Davao City Mayor Sebastian "Baste" Duterte on Monday asked for more time to prepare the necessary documents for his appearance before the Senate impeachment court.

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 12:30pm
Davao City Mayor Sebastian "Baste" Duterte on Monday asked for more time to prepare the necessary documents for his appearance before the Senate impeachment court.

In a letter sent to the Senate impeachment court, the Davao City mayor said he would appear on September 29 to 30 as provided in the subpoena issued to him amid the ongoing impeachment trial of his sister, Vice President Sara Duterte.

"We are in receipt of a letter from Mayor Sebastian Duterte of the City of Davao dated today, requesting that, among others, he be given time, as he requires substantial time to gather, organize, authenticate, and reproduce the subpoena documents, and asks that he be allowed to attend instead of today, tomorrow, and on Wednesday, for him to be allowed to attend on September 29 and 30, that is tomorrow and on Wednesday, which is already covered by the subpoena issued to him," Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis "Chiz" Escudero read the letter.
Escudero immediately granted Duterte's request.
It can be recalled that the impeachment court reset the appearances of Duterte and two others to September 28 to 30 following a conflict in schedule the previous week.

articles.title: Drivers, transport operators begin 3-day strike over fuel price hikes
articles.summary: MANIBELA began a three-day transport strike on Monday, September 28, to protest rising fuel prices.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 12:25pm
Passengers wait for a jeepney ride in Philcoa in Quezon City amid transport strike by Manibela on Sept. 28, 2026.
MANIBELA / Released
MANILA, Philippines — Transport group MANIBELA began a three-day transport strike on Monday, September 28, to protest rising fuel prices.

Around 6 a.m., jeepney drivers, operators and other protesters gathered along University Avenue in Quezon City before proceeding to Philcoa for a demonstration. The group said the strike will run through September 30.
MANIBELA chairperson Mar Valbuena said around 20,000 to 25,000 jeepney drivers from different routes in Metro Manila are expected to participate in the strike.
In a Facebook post, MANIBELA shared images it said showed passengers stranded due to a lack of available jeepneys.
"Pare-pareho pong hindi natin deserve ang ganitong sitwasyon lalo na at sobrang laki ng buwis ang kinukuha sa atin para nakawin lang ng iilan," the group said.
("None of us deserve this situation, especially when so much is taken from us in taxes only to be stolen by a few.")
"Pasensya na po kayo, mabigat pa rin ang presyo ng langis," it added.
("We apologize. Fuel prices remain heavy.")

During the demonstration, Valbuena confronted a person aboard a vehicle bearing a Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) sticker, accusing the person of taking photographs of the license plates of jeepneys participating in the strike.

The LTFRB had earlier warned operators that they could face sanctions if they fail to provide service as required under their franchises during the transport strikes. Acting LTFRB Chairperson Greg Pua Jr. said operators may first be issued a show-cause order and fined at least P5,000 for a first offense.

Pua said succeeding violations may lead to suspension and eventual cancellation of a franchise. The LTFRB has stressed that penalties would depend on evidence showing that an operator failed to provide the required service.
Meanwhile, transport group PISTON is set to begin its own nationwide strike on September 29 and 30, also in protest of rising fuel prices.
PISTON President Mody Floranda has estimated that 70,000 to 100,000 drivers and operators could participate.

articles.title: Cedric Lee, Deniece Cornejo release pending court clearances
articles.summary: BuCor is checking a separate sentence and awaiting court records before their release.

blocks.text: September 28, 2026 | 12:19pm
Composite image shows Cedric Lee, Deniece Cornejo and Vhong Navarro in undated photos.
The STAR / Jesse Bustos, ABS-CBN

MANILA, Philippines — Businessman Cedric Lee and model Deniece Cornejo cannot yet be released despite a Court of Appeals order reducing their sentences, as the Bureau of Corrections said it is still waiting for key court documents and must complete a final records check.

In a statement Monday, September 28, BuCor Director General Gregorio Pio Catapang Jr. said the bureau must first obtain the official entry of judgment docuemnt from the Court of Appeals and a certificate indicating no pending cases from the Taguig City Regional Trial Court.

BuCor said it is formally requesting both documents as part of its standard records validation to ensure that all legal requirements for release of the two respondents in television show host Vhong Navarro's mulling and detention have been met.
"No Entry of Judgement has been issued, therefore it is being requested before the Judicial Records Division of the said court," BuCor said.
The statement came after lawyer Ferdinand Topacio, Cornejo's former counsel, shared with reporters a copy of a Court of Appeals release order covering Cornejo and Lee.
Reduced sentences, separate conviction

Lee and Cornejo were originally sentenced by Taguig RTC Branch 153 to reclusion perpetua, or up to 40 years in prison, after being convicted of serious illegal detention for ransom involving actor-host Vhong Navarro.
The CA Special Seventeenth Division later downgraded the offense to grave coercion and reduced the penalty to a minimum of six months to a maximum of three years, six months and 21 days.
BuCor, however, said its records show that Lee and Cornejo are also serving separate sentences for another grave coercion conviction under Taguig RTC Branch 266.
That sentence, which was affirmed by the CA Ninth Division, carries the same penalty.
Because the two sentences must be served successively, BuCor said their combined prison terms range from a minimum of four years and 21 days to a maximum of seven years and 21 days.
Time credits still part of computation

BuCor's Person Deprived of Liberty Documents and Processing Division said both Lee and Cornejo have accumulated time allowances under Republic Act No. 10592, including Good Conduct Time Allowance and Time Allowance for Study, Teaching and Mentoring.
Lee has been in BuCor custody since May 3, 2024. With 460 days of GCTA, his total credited time stood at three years, 10 months and 29 days as of September 26.
BuCor calculated his presumptive minimum sentence completion date as Feb. 18, 2027, and his maximum sentence completion date as Feb. 18, 2030.
Cornejo, who has been in custody since May 2, 2024, has logged two years, four months and 24 days of actual time served, according to BuCor.
With 440 days of GCTA and 75 days of TASTM, her total credited time stood at three years, nine months and 24 days.
Her presumptive minimum sentence completion date is Dec. 23, 2026, while her maximum sentence completion date is Dec. 23, 2029.

Lee and Cornejo were imprisoned over the 2014 case filed by Navarro, who said he was attacked, restrained, threatened and held by a group that included Lee, which allegedly demanded money in exchange for his release.

Someone must not have gotten enough sleep on the eve of the 30th day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s trial.
Worse, Congressman Bienvenido “Benny” Abante got called out for it — in a moment for the world to see.
Trial presiding officer Chiz Escudero called Abante’s attention on Monday, September 28, when the senator noticed that the congressman’s eyes had been closed for an extended period of time.

“Before calling on Senator Joel Villanueva, may I ask Congressman (Noy) Defensor, (former) congressman (Ace) Barbers to nudge Congressman Benny Abante a bit? It seems he’s tired. He may want to rest somewhere, but not right behind the witness,” Escudero said.
Lead prosecutor Jinky Luistro tried to make light of the situation, saying: “Your Honor, I think he’s praying for us.”
Escudero smiled at the little joke, before saying he doubts that was the case, but also came up with an excuse on behalf of Abante.

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 12:06pm

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Monday assured the public that the government is coordinating with stakeholders to ensure a safe and secure school environment, saying that school shootings are “unacceptable.”
Marcos made the statement during the Recognition of Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) Participating Schools and Education Partners in Pasay City.
“Be assured that the government is working closely with our teachers, parents, barangay workers, and other stakeholders to make schools more secure,” Marcos said during his speech.
“We are committed to providing our youth, our parents, and our community with the knowledge and resources to prevent and respond to school violence,” he added.
Marcos reported that the government hired 10,000 school counselors for the school year 2026-2027, a move to promote a “safe and positive” learning environment for students.
“Hindi katanggap-tanggap 'yung mga pangyayari na nakita natin sa Tacloban, sa Zamboanga, sa South Cotabato,” the President said.
(What happened in Tacloban, Zamboanga, and South Cotabato is unacceptable.)

“Ayaw na ayaw natin na nakikita na hindi tayo nakakasiguro, hindi tayo nakakatiyak na ang ating mga eskwelahan ay ligtas. [Gusto natin ang] mga kabataan ay nasa environment na kaya nilang mag-aral ng mabuti,” he added.
(We do not want to see a situation where we cannot be sure that our schools are safe. We want our young people to be in an environment where they can study well.)

In late June, two students, aged 15 and 14, were involved in a shooting incident that left three people dead and 11 others wounded at San Jose National High School in Barangay San Jose, Tacloban City.
The tragic Zamboanga school shooting left two students dead, including the shooter at the Ateneo de Zamboanga University.
Meanwhile, at least three students, including the shooter himself, died in a shooting incident at Banga National High School in Banga, South Cotabato. —AOL, GMA News

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Monday urged students to remain curious and open to new ideas and perspectives as he attended the recognition ceremony for schools and education partners that participated in the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) in Pasay City.
“To our learners, keep asking questions. Look at things from different points of view. Do not be afraid to change your mind when you learn something new,” Marcos said in his speech.
“To change one's opinion, to change one's view is the prerogative of an intelligent mind,” he added.
Marcos also called on teachers and parents to nurture students' curiosity, encourage them to explore beyond the classroom, and guide them in using technology as a tool for learning.
“Let us teach our children to be intelligent. Let us teach our children to question. Let us teach our children to understand,” the President said.
The Philippines posted its highest-ever mean scores in the PISA in reading, mathematics and science in 2025.
The country recorded mean scores of 373 in science, 371 in mathematics and 367 in reading, up 17, 16 and 20 points, respectively, from its 2022 results.
Based on mean scores, the Philippines ranked above 14 participating countries in science, 16 in mathematics and 18 in reading, according to the Department of Education.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: ‘The same struggles as 100 years ago’: exhibition highlights lives of Sami people in Sweden
articles.summary:
Show at Kin Museum in Kiruna marks handover of long-awaited report on abuses committed by the state against the Indigenous people

From a detailed multi-perspectival drawing of reindeer to…

blocks.text: From a detailed multi-perspectival drawing of reindeer to written accounts of belief systems and childbirth, Johan Turi’s work offers unparalleled insight into his life as a Sami person living in northern Sweden at the start of the 20th century.

In the face of racist discrimination, land disputes and the spectre of encroaching industry, Turi wanted his 1910 book Muitalus sámiid birra (An Account of the Sami) to set the record straight about the lives of Europe’s only recognised Indigenous people.
Turi is widely regarded as the first Sami author to write about Sami life in his own language, but until now his pioneering works had not been on display for almost 100 years.

blocks.caption: The artist Outi Pieski, whose art is featured in the Johan Turi exhibition at Kin. Photograph: Johan Ylitalo/Kin Museum of Contemporary Art

blocks.text: To mark the handover to the Swedish government this week of a long-awaited report by the Truth Commission for the Sami People on abuses committed by the state against the Sami, his writings, drawings, paintings and Duodji (traditional Sami handicraft) now form the centre of an exhibition at the Kin Museum of Contemporary Art in Kiruna, the area in which he used to live.
The title of the exhibition, On the Ugly and the Beautiful, draws from a quote by Turi, who died in 1936, about his belief that everything, positive and negative, has a place to be shown.
His work is on display alongside two contemporary artists, Outi Pieski and Johanna Minde.

The museum’s director, Maria Lind, said An Account of the Sami, which was published in Sami and Danish before being translated into Swedish seven years later, is “about Sami life, small and big – external and inner life”.

Turi was born in Guovdageainnu (Kautokeino), the Norwegian part of Sápmi, in 1854 but as the imposition of formal national borders began to have a bigger impact on the lives of the Sami, his family, who were reindeer herders, moved to Kiruna.

“He had dreamed about writing a book about the Sami with the purpose of making the population in Sweden understand how difficult it was for the Sami because those were difficult years,” Lind said, citing the arrival of settlers, industry, including mining, and the railway.
“He wanted the king to read his book because he felt if the king knew then things would change. Most likely the king did not read his book, but it became a success,” she added.

blocks.caption: An artwork by Outi Pieski at the Kin Museum. Photograph: Johan Ylitalo/Kin Museum

blocks.text: The problems facing Sami people today are not dissimilar to those Turi would recognise. Industry – especially the search for rare earth minerals and wind energy – is an ever-increasing threat to reindeer herding and nature. Anti-Sami rhetoric is on the rise, including from political leaders, despite the seeming progress symbolised by the truth commission and its report, which will be presented on Wednesday. Similar commissions have also been held in Norway and Finland.
But unlike in Turi’s time, there is now the escalating impact of the climate crisis, particularly visible in the Arctic and northern regions.

blocks.caption: The ládjogahpir, a traditional hat historically worn by Sami women. Photograph: Johan Ylitalo/Kin Museum

blocks.text: As the report, which is intended to form the basis for reparation and reconciliation discussions, is handed over at Mid Sweden University in Staare, the Kin Museum will put on a special tour of the works, after which there will be a reading of testimonies at the culture house next door.

Pieski, who lives on the Finnish side of Sápmi, said she grew up with Turi’s writings and drawings, in which she sees the paper as the land itself. “And then humans, animals, everything is grounded on that paper,” she said.

“It’s not a western way of seeing a landscape as a beautiful view that you look at from a distance. But the actual place where you are, physically placed, and you are an active member of this network of land.”

Her research and exploration with Eeva-Kristiina Nylander around the subject of the ládjogahpir, a traditional hat historically worn by Sami women, is also part of the exhibition. Their work has helped to bring it back into use. It has, said Pieski, become a “new symbol for decolonial feminism”.
She said that in many ways Turi’s work started the current process of truth and reconciliation by writing about life and Sami culture from his point of view.

“It’s very sad that we are kind of in the same spot still now, 100 years later,” she said. “And I know the same struggles are still existing that Johan Turi brought out with the fight for industrial land use and so on.
“No nation can exist without their own spoken or written histories. Ignoring it is a very simple colonial tool [that does] not give existence to one nation that we are here.”

articles.title: Ed Miliband to acknowledge Labour’s former stance on Palestine fell short
articles.summary:
Foreign secretary will tell party’s conference ‘we are not here to accept the status quo but to change it’

Ed Miliband will tell campaigners and party members who raised the plight of…

blocks.text: Ed Miliband will tell campaigners and party members who raised the plight of Palestinians they were right that Labour’s approach had not been enough, saying he was heeding the calls of millions of people by imposing sanctions on Israeli settlements.

The foreign secretary will tell the Labour party conference that the government will take more explicitly progressive foreign policy positions under Andy Burnham, and that the UK will be a leader among like-minded countries in a new age of diplomacy.

He will say there is a “fundamental and wider lesson from Israel and Palestine about how we have changed our approach as a party”, saying Labour will succeed “because of, not in spite of, our progressive values”.
He will talk of the start of a new and more muscular foreign policy. “We are not here to accept the status quo but to change it at home and abroad,” he will say.
The party’s conference hall was often the scene of fierce opposition to Keir Starmer’s stance on Israel and Palestine in Labour’s final year of opposition and early in government.

blocks.caption: The foreign secretary, Ed Miliband. Photograph: Wiktor Szymanowicz/Future Publishing/Getty Images

blocks.text: Since becoming foreign secretary, Miliband has announced sweeping sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements against a backdrop of increasing settler violence in the West Bank, which has resulted in 12 countries – including France and Canada – announcing they would also impose sanctions.
The Guardian understands Miliband will say in his speech that the sanctions marked a definitive change in how Labour will approach the situation in the Middle East.
“I want to say to the millions of people in this country and indeed elsewhere who have been moved and outraged by the plight of the Palestinian people: we hear you, you were right,” he will say.

“And under Andy’s leadership, we have reset our approach. We call out ethnic cleansing by the settler terrorists in the West Bank. We call out the evidence of war crimes in Gaza. We call out Israel’s illegal occupation of Palestine. And we match words with actions.
after newsletter promotion

“We will ban the import of goods from illegal settlements. We will disrupt the supply lines of British finance, British construction and British services for illegal settlements. And when it comes to the attempt to destroy the two-state solution, this party, this movement, this government, says ‘we will not let you succeed’.”

Miliband will pay tribute to those who have campaigned against the Israeli onslaught in Gaza, though his warm words are likely to raise questions about whether the government will review the proscription of Palestine Action. Police arrested a number of demonstrators outside the conference hall on Sunday.
“The bonds of solidarity between the British people and those who yearn for peace in Israel and Palestine are too strong to be broken,” Miliband will say.
“Our decision to act mobilised the international community, country after country. This is how to make change happen in today’s world. Doing what is right and galvanising others to act too.”

Miliband will say in his first speech to the party conference as foreign secretary that cooperation in imposing sanctions will be the beginning of a new bond with “likeminded countries” such as France and Canada, though it is also likely to be interpreted as being more willing to sideline the US.

Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, has made an explicit argument for middle powers to do more to build alliances with each other outside traditional structures, and was direct in his desire to forge closer ties with and among European countries in a speech in Brussels earlier this month.

A source close to Miliband said that would be a key theme of his time in office. “Britain’s interests are served by standing up for our values on the world stage. Our ability to build coalitions on big global issues depends on our ability to bring countries with us,” he will say.
“This Israel/Palestine reset is a sign of how we want to do business. We are going to be propositional in bringing countries with us on the issues we really care about.”

articles.title: Reality Fracture’s best cards in Magic: The Gathering
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines – Magic: The Gathering’s (MTG) multiversal saga headlined by Jace Beleren is coming to a head with its latest Standard expansion, Reality Fracture releasing on October 2, 2026.…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Magic: The Gathering’s (MTG) multiversal saga headlined by Jace Beleren is coming to a head with its latest Standard expansion, Reality Fracture releasing on October 2, 2026.

What if the Multiverse existed without the suffering, Eldrazi, and Phyrexians that shaped its history? Reality Fracture explores those possibilities through the Echoverse, a warped reflection of the Multiverse created by Jace.

That idea extends to the set’s cards, with familiar characters and concepts receiving drastically different versions of themselves. From changes in abilities and effects to characters taking on entirely different colors, Reality Fracture puts a new spin on some of Magic’s most recognizable faces.
As the global release comes closer, here are some of the cards worth keeping an eye on as Reality Fracture makes its way into players’ hands.
RELATED STORY: Magic: The Gathering Foundations Commander decks explained
Blue
The Theorist, Jace Beleren
Realistically, the big bad of this set and the protagonist of MTG for the longest time, The Theorist, Jace Beleren acts as the set’s poster boy, and with good reason.

With a built-in draw engine that gains you a card during each opponent’s draw phase, an ability that leaves a creature behind, a way to interact with a creature or artifact under each opponent’s control, and a pseudo-game-winning ultimate that draws cards and strengthens your creatures, The Theorist puts theories into practice, creating card advantage without skipping a beat.

While it’s obvious that multiplayer formats like Commander were taken into consideration with the “each opponent” wording found in his abilities, the real heat comes from the alternate versions of cards found throughout the set.
Perfected Theory
Perfected Theory lives up to its namesake and turns into an efficient piece of removal, while making combat more difficult for your opponent.
With the prevalence of prowess-based strategies in literally every format, Perfected Theory is the card you have to play around once you see blue.
Turning a normal turn into a blowout is a common sight in Modern Prowess, and doing it sooner makes the deck a faster matchup than it normally is.
Samut, Tyrant of Naktamun
Cited as being the card that would probably ruin competitive Commander, Samut, Tyrant of Naktamun is one of many echoed pairs found throughout the expansion.
While its red counterpart gives all creatures you control haste, the blue Samut doesn’t let your opponent react, granting all your instants and sorceries split second.

There’s no denying that it would shake up the meta in one way or another. Being blue, though, does make it more relevant in older formats, serving as a pitchable card for Force of Will and Force of Negation.
Green
Hexhaven Invigorator
A riff on Phyrexian Obliterator from way back in the early days of New Phyrexia, Hexhaven Invigorator is one of the most–if not the most–broken cards in the set.
Green continues to show why it’s the creature color with an efficient beater, with four green mana already creating a 6/6 threat with vigilance, but the effect makes it a bit over the top.

For each damage that Hexhaven Invigorator takes, it lets its owner get any land from their deck tapped. While it would be fine getting basic lands, having the flexibility to get tech lands or win-cons like Valakut, The Molten Pinnacle make this card a must remove threat.
Carnivorous Cultivator
Fetchlands are a quintessential part of MTG as formats get deeper, and in slower formats, a creature that can recur lands while accruing value is always worth watching.

Carnivorous Cultivator joins green’s roster of land searchers alongside Elvish Reclaimer and Crop Rotation. While it may be on the slower side, being able to recur lands with a creature that’s difficult to block thanks to deathtouch can generate plenty of value over the course of a game.
Pia, Aether Ascetic

Pia, Aether Ascetic is an enchantment tutor in colors that shouldn’t be able to find them that easily. While green does have a semblance of enchantment support, this is usually through Aura effects needing a creature in play.

Pia ignores the normal play pattern established by green, giving its user the flexibility to get key enchantments as it enters the battlefield like removal such as Oblivion Ring or a bomb like Omniscience.
Black
Darklight Phoenix
An alternate take on Arclight Phoenix, Darklight Phoenix spins the entire Arclight effect of coming back from the graveyard ready to attack.

Triggering off multiple instances of instants and sorceries and shifting over to deaths puts Darklight in a unique spot. Unlike its predecessor, it counts instances specifically creature deaths in general and not just those on your side. The original Arclight Phoenix strategy dominated the Standard metagame and is still a valid strategy in Pioneer, but Darklight Phoenix has a bright future ahead of itself once the right home materializes.
Sanctum Lurker
Cards that break rules are always bound to be broken, and Sanctum Lurker breaks the foundational rule of planeswalkers existing even without any loyalty counters.
While it has an awkward statline for its mana cost, it allows Superfriends decks to not only keep their planeswalker army safe during combat, but also enables some potentially broken synergies.
One example is Gideon Jura. With Sanctum Lurker in play, you can continuously use Gideon’s plus-two ability to force your opponent’s creatures to attack it.

Normally, a planeswalker with no loyalty counters would be sent to the graveyard. Sanctum Lurker prevents that from happening, allowing Gideon to remain on the battlefield and use the same ability again on the following turn.
Lich’s Relic
Equipment in MTG is only as good as the creature wielding it, but in the case of Lich’s Relic, its value when it enters.
For an additional two mana upon entry, Lich’s Relic lets its user destroy a creature or planeswalker per player currently in the game.
While it resembles the common Crude Bent Blade from The Hobbit, being able to bypass player hexproof and destroy planeswalkers justifies its higher rarity.
It gets even better when the artifact is cycled with cards like Goblin Welder or Goblin Engineer, letting the destruction effect happen more than once.
Red
Curse-Marred Demon
An alternate version of Rune-Scarred Demon, Curse-Marred Demon is a decent beater with a tutor stapled onto it.
At 4/4 for four mana, this red Demon with flying and trample enters the battlefield with a Gamble stapled onto it.
This lets you search for any card from your deck in exchange for discarding a card at random.

A searcher attached to a sizable body is always a great thing to have, and with how prevalent graveyard strategies are, as well as the existence of abilities like Madness and Mayhem, getting a guaranteed spell at a discount is always a good.
Identity Echo
Polymorph and other similar effects are strong in the context of MTG, oftentimes cheating something unfair into play way before it normally should. Identity Echo continues that trend.
Similar to the play patterns established by the red sorcery Indomitable Creativity, Identity Echo could transform any creature or planeswalker into another one found in the deck.
With the right deck design, normally weak tokens like Dwarves from Dwarven Mine or even Jace tokens could turn into game-ending threats like Emrakul or Nicol Bolas.
Pyre Rhymer
Taking a page out of Strixhaven with the Prepared mechanic, Pyre Rhymer offers a red ritual effect in the same vein as Molten Tide’s originator, High Tide.
Apart from coming with a 3/3 body for three mana that gets bigger with each noncreature spell cast thanks to prowess, it also comes prepared with Molten Tide ready to be cast on the following turn.

While there are no obvious homes for it at the time of writing, costing three mana in a color that could potentially have it ready by turn two with the various ritual effects available makes it something to be wary of.
White
Guiding Hydra
Hydras are often found in the green spectrum of MTG, with white being a supplementary color, like Progenitus. Guiding Hydra changes all that.

Reality Fracture breaks the normal Hydra mold, featuring a creature that not only acts as a mana sink from turn two onwards but also provides an anthem effect every turn, granting each other creature on its controller’s side of the battlefield +1/+1 counters.
This is something that white go-wide strategies would gladly accept.
Flickering Hound
As an alternate version of Displacer Kitten, Flickering Hound at four mana enables degenerate combos given the right circumstances.
In lieu of noncreature spells triggering a flicker effect for nonland permanents, including creatures, Flickering Hound does the same for creatures, flickering another creature upon casting a spell.

While the combo applications aren’t as wide, being able to generate value from other creatures entering the battlefield in dedicated creature decks is something to be wary of, making this a potential must-have for any creature-based Commander deck with white down the line.
Loyal Tutor
One-mana tutors have always been strong in their own right, with Worldly Tutor and Enlightened Tutor being two notable examples.
This set introduces Loyal Tutor specifically for planeswalkers.

In the right deck, a one-mana silver-bullet finder is invaluable, and with strategies that can crumble under the presence of key walkers like Teferi, Time Raveler and Narset, Parter of Veils, Loyal Tutor will definitely be seeing play in planeswalker-centric strategies.
Multicolor
Avatar of Burgeoning Echoes

Avatar of Burgeoning Echoes seems like a boring card, letting you empower Jace tokens as you play lands. As Jace ticks up thanks to empower you get to occasionally draw a card after playing two lands or mill one card a turn.

As you move into formats with fetchlands, this steady stream of advantage can get overwhelming. Even with just one additional card per turn, decks like the Azorius Loki strategy in Modernshow that every draw matters.
It also helps that there’s a planeswalker that would need to be dealt with even without the Avatar.
Solitary Cell
Red-white control decks have it good with all the removal options being printed recently, and Solitary Cell just strengthens already existing strategies.
On entry, it removes any nonland permanent with mana value three or less, while its cycling effect lets you turn excess legends into value.
Solitary Cell also makes Oswald Fiddlebender-based decks more fluid, giving them a removal option at two mana while continuing the artifact chain.
Aerid Konstrari
The Konstrari (R/G) is what happens when Jace alters the Prismari (U/R) school of thought, ditching instants and sorceries for artifacts.
This Gruul (R/G)-coded Elder Sphinx is an efficient cost beater that practically just costs three mana when you take its Heartwood token into consideration.

Apart from being an infinite enters-the-battlefield trigger with Food Chain in Commander, it also lends itself to being a fun build-around card considering there will always be artifact synergies laying around.
Special Mentions
Emrakul, the Exigent Doom
Emrakul is the only colorless card in the set and a fitting endgame in Reality Fracture’s story.
Emrakul, the Exigent Doom does two things and does them really well. It accelerates your mana generation by turning any of your lands into two colorless mana for use in the future.
This effect can give you a late-game threat your opponents have to be wary of.
Somewhat of a game-ender while still supporting big-mana strategies, Emrakul is going to be a card you’ll want in your collection regardless of your format.
Tarmogoyf
Once regarded as one of the strongest cards in MTG, Tarmogoyf finally enters the Standard card pool after an absence of almost two decades.
While it may not be the titan it once was, being in a lower-power environment in Standard, and to a minor extent Pioneer, may let it resemble the terror it once was.
Times have changed, with removal improving heavily, but that won’t stop players from forcing Tarmogoyf when there are better things to do with two mana.
Is Reality Fracture a good set competitively, casually, and for collectors?
While Jace Beleren’s time in MTG is legendary, from the onset, Reality Fracture is shaping up to be an all-timer set, complete with a mechanic that could see use years from now in Empower.
The card quality present has considerations for every format, with some cards like Samut, Tyrant of Naktamun sure to shake things up once they become legal.
Even the presence of Tarmogoyf in the format gives longtime players a reason to celebrate, as they can dust off their old copies that have been lying in wait.
MTG’s second-to-last set of the year has all the tools to make an impact across every format.
Whether it’s through Empower, power creep, or the sheer number of new tools available to players, Reality Fracture has plenty to offer players of every caliber.
For collectors, the set’s special printings, alternate versions, and bundles add another layer of appeal beyond the cards themselves.
Reality Fracture is set to have its global release on October 2, 2026, with prereleases happening from September 25, 2026 onwards.
RELATED STORY: Inside the Reality Fracture Multiverse Reforged commander deck

articles.title: OpenAI, Anthropic CEOs called to appear at Australian AI probe
articles.summary: The Medicare breach, condemned by Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, is one of the highest-profile incidents of AI agents accessing external systems outside the US

blocks.text: LEADER. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese reacts during a press conference in Sydney, Australia, in Sydney, Australia, on September 12, 2025.
Hollie Adams/Reuters
The Medicare breach, condemned by Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, is one of the highest-profile incidents of AI agents accessing external systems outside the US

items: The CEOs of OpenAI and Anthropic have been summoned to an Australian Senate inquiry following a breach of the country's health system by an OpenAI bot.
The incident, condemned by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, may lead to stricter AI regulations in Australia, impacting US-Australia relations.
The inquiry aims to address the implications of AI on various sectors and demands accountability from the tech leaders regarding effective regulation.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

SYDNEY, Australia – The CEOs of OpenAI and Anthropic have been called to appear at an Australian Senate inquiry on AI, the head of the probe said on Sunday, September 27, days after the revelation that a rogue OpenAI bot had hacked the country’s health-system database.
The Medicare breach, condemned by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, is one of the highest-profile incidents of AI agents accessing external systems outside the US.

OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Anthropic’s Dario Amodei have been sent written requests to appear at the inquiry, which is to hold public hearings in the capital Canberra on Thursday, said a spokesperson for Senator Sarah Hanson-Young of the Australian Greens party, who chairs the probe.
OpenAI and Anthropic did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside business hours.

The OpenAI agent’s incursion on one of the country’s most used government agencies may prompt Albanese’s Labor government to toughen AI-specific laws it is readying for next year, adding pressure to Australia-US relations already tested by Canberra’s ban on social media for teens, tech policy experts say.
The Senate inquiry is examining the potential impacts of AI and data centres on Australian communities, industries, water and energy. It is one of several state and federal probes into AI.

“There are serious questions for Sam Altman to answer about the OpenAI hack of Australian government websites,” Hanson-Young said in a statement. Altman and Amodei “must front up, face the Senate’s questions and have an honest conversation about what effective, lasting regulation of this industry should look like”, she said.
Albanese, who revealed the June breach of Medicare on Thursday, called it “unacceptable”, saying he had voiced “extreme concern” to Altman.

OpenAI says it only learned of the breach — one of at least four of Australian government websites — in August. It says the incident was not intentional and did not compromise any private information. – Rappler.com

articles.title: House prosecutors withdraw request for Sara Duterte to admit bank accounts
articles.summary: The House prosecution panel on Monday withdrew its request for admission seeking Vice President Sara Duterte"s acknowledgment that she owned the bank accounts whose records were ordered submitted by…

blocks.text: Published September 28, 2026 11:33am

The House prosecution panel on Monday withdrew its request for admission seeking Vice President Sara Duterte’s acknowledgment that she owned the bank accounts whose records were ordered submitted by the banks to the Senate impeachment court.

In a manifestation during the 28th day of the impeachment trial, House prosecutor Chel Diokno of Akbayan party-list instead asked the defense to agree to stipulations, or agreements, on the authenticity of the bank records.
The proposed stipulations include:

items: that the bank accounts exist;
that the bank account records were produced by the banks pursuant to the subpoenas issued by the Senate impeachment court; and
that the bank records are genuine and authentic copies of records maintained and produced by the subject banks.

blocks.text: In putting forward the stipulations, Diokno argued that the accuracy of the bank documents “is not genuinely in dispute.”

“The request for admission is not being invoked to alter the burden of proof or to compel the respondent to establish the prosecution’s case and will not have that effect. Its purpose is simply to narrow the issues and avoid the needless presentation of witnesses and evidence on matters that are not genuinely disputed,” Diokno said during Day 30 of the impeachment trial.
“To be clear, the respondent has not made any claim that they are fake or fabricated. We will withdraw our request for admission if the respondent will agree to this,” Diokno added.

In response, defense team lead counsel Shiela Sison cited jurisprudence, or existing court decisions, from 1905, 1937 and 1969 that protect a respondent’s right against self-incrimination, in addition to the Constitution.
“The court has consistently said that an admission is actually akin to a testimony, that is why it is called an admission," she said.

"And if the Constitution prohibits compulsion for a respondent or accused to testify for himself or herself, the request for admission should likewise be prohibited here [in the impeachment],” Sison added.

The Senate impeachment court will still rule on the prosecution’s initial request for admission to provide guidance to both parties, according to presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero.— MCG, GMA News

MANILA, Philippines — Consumers could get an LPG price cut of at least P3 per kilogram this week, only to face a much larger increase days later as global costs push higher.

Arnel Ty, president of the LPG Marketers Association, said Monday, September 28, that prices were expected to fall by at least P3 per kilogram following the government's three-month suspension of excise taxes on liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene.
But Ty also warned of a possible P10-to-P15-per-kilogram increase as early as October 3, depending on the final computation of world-market prices.
President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed Executive Order 125 on September 25, granting the temporary excise-tax relief.
Ty said the industry learned through coordination with the Bureau of Customs that the tax-driven reduction would be implemented within the week.
Republic Gas Corp., or Regasco, will cut its LPG price by P3 per kilogram starting Wednesday, September 30.

The reduction could reach P3.36 per kilogram once the 12% value-added tax imposed on the excise tax is included, Ty said. The Department of Energy has yet to formalize the final equivalent price adjustment.

"Sa ngayon, Department of Energy na po ang magpo-formalize kung ano po ang dapat na equivalent po niyan," Ty told dzMM. ("For now, the Department of Energy will formalize the appropriate equivalent reduction.")
Relief may be short-lived
The tax relief could be quickly overwhelmed by a projected increase in LPG prices in early October.
Ty said the final adjustment would be calculated on October 1 and could take effect October 3.
He attributed the expected increase to higher world-market prices and shipping premiums amid geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
"Lubhang napakataas po ng inangat ng premium cost. It is almost $200 plus per metric ton," Ty said. ("The premium cost has risen sharply. It is almost $200-plus per metric ton.")
The excise-tax suspension will remain in effect despite the expected market-driven increase, potentially cushioning what consumers would otherwise pay.
Under the directive, the tax relief can last for up to three months. The excise tax may be restored one week after the one-month average price of Dubai crude falls below the $80-per-barrel benchmark.

articles.title: [Newspoint] All politics
articles.summary: The trial is increasingly revealing itself as more, much more, political than legal business. All too obviously, just about any intervention, any utterance, any vote cast by a senator-judge is…

blocks.text: The trial is increasingly revealing itself as more, much more, political than legal business. All too obviously, just about any intervention, any utterance, any vote cast by a senator-judge is politically loaded.

items: The court has taken the view that four senators are incapable of doing their duty as judges and, therefore, should not be allowed to vote Duterte’s fate.
The number of senator-judges was reduced from 24 to 20, lowering the two-thirds threshold for conviction from 16 to 14 votes.
The trial is perceived as politically charged, with significant implications for Duterte's future and the integrity of the impeachment process.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

The impeachment court has ruled: 14 votes to find the Vice President, Sara Duterte, guilty. She is on trial in the Senate on charges of, among others, embezzling taxpayer pesos in the hundreds of millions and of hiring an assassin to kill the President and his wife and his cousin the former Speaker.

The court has taken the view that four senators are incapable of doing their duty as judges and, therefore, should not be allowed to vote Duterte’s fate. Two of these four are detained without bail on charges of plunder, one is a fugitive from justice, and one is out of the country on an indefinite medical leave, although also under preliminary investigation herself on suspicion of plunder and graft. All four are minority senators.

Since, with those disqualifications, the number of senator-judges comes down from 24 to 20, the two-thirds threshold provided by the Constitution comes down too, proportionately, from 16 to 14. That’s the math that shall apply.

It seems a foregone conclusion that Duterte’s lawyers will go to the Supreme Court to question its constitutionality, such being their wont. But is it the right time? Will the court, if it intervenes at all, do it before the threshold is actually applied to convict Duterte or afterward, when there might be an immediate justiciable case for wrongful conviction?

A funny thing, by the way, happened on the way to the vote. Mark Villar did not join sister Camille and the five other capable senators in the minority in boycotting it. Camille even shed tears to prelude the boycott. She took the floor, rare for her, and poured her heart out for the two plunder indictees for having been called, as she had heard it, “plunderers,” already presumed guilty. She actually had heard wrong, and her ears were straightened out promptly.

At any rate, her brother did vote; he opposed lowering the threshold. Still, while he may have simply chosen the normal, undramatic, dry way of expressing dissent, breaking with family and party meant breaking from a herd that all these nearly three months of trial had marched closely together, in lockstep, and in the same direction. That’s why the break set off speculations about his standing with the minority. Those speculations are, without doubt, wishful ones, as might be expected in a highly politically charged case.

Ah, but Chiz Escudero — trust him to be cool, decisive, quick, clever, and, yes, suitably learned. He asks critical questions that have gone unasked and refines and sharpens vague or technically couched questions, in that way making himself a decided help to the lay multitudes like me watching the trial on television or online. All in all, I’d say, he has run the trial smoothly, prudently, fairly.

In fact, he even manages to make himself not look bad when he should have looked worse, say, after making a bad call, as he precisely, and prematurely, did at the outset on the very issue of the threshold vote. Upon assuming the presidency of the court, he declared that two-thirds equals 16 of the 24 senators makes for the immutable math prescribed by the Constitution.
When his pronouncement was put to a vote, he stuck to his guns, siding with the minority, in this one instance anyway. But once voted down, he conceded to the majority.

“While the chair takes exception to this decision, the chair nonetheless accepts it as a judgment of this court and is bound to give it effect. The presiding officer, after all, is not the court. He is merely the custodian of the process, not the proprietor of it,” he said. He was speaking in illeism, referring to himself in the third person (“the chair,” “the presiding officer,” “he”), as Julius Caesar did writing about himself crossing the Rubicon. And, I must say, with genuine amusement, the style quite suits him.

But before I forget myself and blindly go overboard, let me point out that Escudero’s gracious concession was a mere one-off, a procedural one-off; it commits him to nothing else. In fact, although situationally open to the danger of slip-ups as court president, having to make spot rulings in the course of the trial, he does not seem to me to have ever given himself away.

But then again, who am I kidding? The trial is increasingly revealing itself as more, much more, political than legal business. All too obviously, just about any intervention, any utterance, any vote cast by a senator-judge is politically loaded.

Which is singularly unfortunate, since, even under the rigors of a regular court trial, this impeachment case needs little proving. An acquittal thus opens up an opportunity for the impeached to continue plaguing the nation with the ruinous ways for which she was impeached in the first place. – Rappler.com

MANILA, Philippines – Commuters will pay higher fares for public utility vehicles (PUVs) starting Monday, September 28, after the Department of Transportation (DOTr) lifted the suspension on fare increases approved by the Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB).
The fare increases were originally set to take effect in March but were suspended by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. amid the conflict in the Middle East, which drove up global oil prices.
The minimum fare for jeepneys increased from P13 to P14. The rate for each succeeding kilometer rose to P2 from P1.80.

blocks.caption: FARE GUIDE. The table shows the fare for public utility jeepneys, effective September 28, 2026.

items: Ordinary buses: P15 for the first 5 kilometers, plus P2.49 for every succeeding kilometer
Airconditioned buses: P18 for the first 5 kilometers, plus P2.98 for every succeeding kilometer.

blocks.text: For provincial buses, the first 5 kilometers on ordinary buses will cost P12. The succeeding-kilometer rates are:

items: Ordinary: P2.20
Airconditioned: P2.45
Deluxe: P2.60

Luxury: P3.35

blocks.text: The base fare for ride-hailing cars or transportation network vehicle services (TNVS) increased by P20 across all vehicle types. Here’s a comparison of the old and new base fare:

P2P bus fares increased by 15% from the existing rates, depending on the route.

items: Traditional UV Express: P2.60 per kilometer for traditional UV Express

blocks.text: The flag-down rates for taxis will also increase depending on the type of taxi, as listed below:

articles.title: Ukraine, South Korea relations sour over North Korean POWs
articles.summary: South Korea has accused Ukraine of breaching a confidentiality agreement over the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war — and of denying the deal's existence. Seoul has demanded an apology.

image.caption: 'I do not know why the Ukrainian side broke the agreement and made the matter public, but it is very disappointing,' said Lee Jae MyungImage: Anthony Wallace/AFP

blocks.text: South Korea has demanded an official apology from Ukraine after accusing Kyiv of breaching — and then reportedly denying the existence of — a confidentiality agreement regarding the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war (POWs) to Seoul.
Last week, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced the transfer in an address to the United Nations General Assembly in New York, adding that the soldiers were "not easy to capture alive."
Hours later, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung wrote on social media: "I do not know why the Ukrainian side broke the agreement and made the matter public, but it is very disappointing."
On Sunday, the South Korean consternation was made official when Seong Ghi-hong, senior presidential secretary for public relations, demanded "an official explanation and apology."

"The presidential office expresses strong regret over Ukraine's unilateral disclosure and its subsequent false announcement that there had not been a non-disclosure agreement," Seong said in a statement.
"It is in itself a very serious matter that … seriously undermines trust between the two governments and gravely damages friendly relations between the two countries."
Seong said Seoul was "considering additional measures that may be necessary regarding this matter," but did not specify what they might be.
Why a new Russia-North Korea road bridge worries Ukraine
Ukraine: When were the North Korean soldiers captured?

The North Korean soldiers were captured by Ukrainian forces in Russia's Kursk region in January 2025 — two of around 14,000 North Korean troops deployed to the area to help halt and push back a surprise Ukrainian incursion.

Ukrainian intelligence estimates that around 3,000 North Korean troops were killed and another 1,500 injured, with the rest still stationed on Russian territory. To date, no North Korean troops are believed to have operated on Ukrainian territory itself.
Ukrainian troops reported that North Korean soldiers who were surrounded or injured on the battlefield preferred to die by suicide than surrender — and only two were captured.

Under President Lee, who has attempted to improve relations with the North, South Korea has appeared hesitant to take custody of the pair. But, under Article 3 of the South Korean constitution, North Koreans are still considered citizens of the South and are permitted to live in the South.
South Korea is an ally of Ukraine, albeit one which has so far only provided non-lethal aid. But Kyiv has been pressing Seoul to provide advanced air defense systems.
Last month, President Zelenskyy claimed that up to 50,000 more North Korean troops could be deployed to Russia.

articles.title: LIVE UPDATES: Impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte
articles.summary: Bookmark this page for Rappler's comprehensive coverage of Vice President Sara Duterte's impeachment trial at the Senate

blocks.text: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte — the first Philippine public official to be impeached twice by the House of Representatives — began at 2 pm on Monday, July 6.

There are four articles of impeachment against Duterte involving alleged misuse of confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery of Department of Education officials, and grave threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his family.

Only 21 out of 24 senator-judges are physically present. Senator Bato dela Rosa remains in hiding as he faces an International Criminal Court arrest warrant over Rodrigo Duterte’s drug war, Senator Jinggoy Estrada has been detained and suspended in connection with a plunder case, and Senator Rodante Marcoleta surrendered to authorities as he also faces a plunder case.
On this page, we bring you the latest updates, analyses, videos, and photos as the trial of the Vice President unfolds.

blocks.text: Sep 23, 2026 9:07 PM PHT
Litigator counters Poa’s argument against lowering voting threshold

“Moving the threshold in terms of impeachment because it serves accountability does not have to mean moving the threshold elsewhere — bogeyman ‘yun,” litigator and Free Legal Assistance member Raffy Aquino said in a Rappler panel discussion during Day 29 of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial on Wednesday, September 23.

The comment was made following defense lawyer Michael Poa’s argument that lowering the voting threshold for impeachment could have consequences on other constitutional provisions, such as revoking or extending martial law, expulsion of a member of the Senate, or amending the Constitution itself. – Rhen Peñada
Sep 23, 2026 8:54 PM PHT
A Villar split: Why is Mark Villar breaking ranks with sister Camille?
Two roads diverged in the Senate on Wednesday, September 23 — and the Villar siblings took different ones.

Senator-judge Mark Villar broke ranks with his sister, Senator-judge Camille Villar, and the Senate minority bloc in a surprise vote on two key motions during the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
Sep 23, 2026 7:36 PM PHT
Change in voting threshold not yet a ‘justiciable controversy’

Litigator and Free Legal Assistance Group member Raffy Aquino stressed on Wednesday, September 23, that the change in the voting threshold for the impeachment trial does not yet present a “justiciable controversy” that could be reviewed by the Supreme Court (SC).
“There is no injury yet. The Vice President still remains as vice president. And there is no vote yet on the conviction or acquittal,” he explained.
Aquino added that while the SC’s power of judicial review has been expanded to preserve its checking function, it remains limited and requires an actual controversy and grave abuse of discretion.
He added that if the previous threshold of 16 votes is still met, “then there is no controversy” since the conviction would stand.

Based on his experience as an “occasional constitutional litigator,” Aquino said the SC “does not easily lend itself to obstructions,” emphasizing that there must first be an actual controversy before the Court could intervene. – Rena Eñano
Sep 23, 2026 6:14 PM PHT
Why did Mark Villar vote differently from sister Camille?

Following the Senate impeachment court vote on the conviction voting threshold, litigator Raffy Aquino says on Wednesday, September 23, that the Villar siblings Mark and Camille showed one of two things: they either “demonstrated how it is to vote according to one’s conscience,” or it was a strategy to have a foot on either side of the door.

articles.title: 'We will not be intimidated': Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc chief after reported white nationalist gathering
articles.summary: B.C. politicians and leaders are denouncing an apparent gathering of white nationalists on the Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc reserve near Kamloops, B.C. Kúkpi7 Rosanne Casimir says the nation received…

image.caption: Rosanne Casimir, Chief of the Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc, says this incident will not deter the community from 'gathering, reflecting, or honoring our survivors and the children who returned home.' (Ben Nelms/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia

B.C. politicians and leaders are denouncing an apparent gathering of white nationalists on the Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc reserve near Kamloops, B.C. Kúkpi7 Rosanne Casimir says the nation received reports Sunday morning of roughly 30 masked men on the reserve.
B.C. politicians and leaders condemn reported gathering, calling it 'disgraceful' and 'hateful'
B.C. politicians and leaders are denouncing an apparent gathering of white nationalists on the Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc reserve, just east of Kamloops.

Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc Kúkpi7 Rosanne Casimir says the nation received reports Sunday morning of a gathering of roughly 30 men, donning white face masks and black caps, standing together around the reserve while hoisting flags over their shoulders.

In a press release, Casimir said "individuals associated with Second Sons Canada, a group linked to white supremacist and white nationalist ideology, have been seen and documented within our community."
"White supremacy will not instill fear in generations of survivors and intergenerational survivors who have already carried fear for far too long," said Casimir in the release.

Images circulating on social media appear to show logos on flags and clothing affiliated with Second Sons Canada. However, CBC News has not been able to independently verify the identities of the individuals or their group affiliations.
Casimir told CBC News that the reserve's security told the men they were not permitted to gather and asked them to leave. However, they did not leave until RCMP were called and arrived at the scene.

items: Leaders in B.C. release joint statement condemning anti-Indigenous racism

blocks.text: CBC News reached out to the RCMP but did not hear back before publication.

Speaking at the Vancouver International Airport Sunday afternoon, NDP Leader David Eby said there has been a rise "in this kind of white nationalist behaviour" in B.C., adding that more needs to be done "to fight it."

"This is just disgraceful, disgusting behaviour. It's very clear that these people were trying to intimidate, make people feel fearful," said the premier, adding that the men in face masks would face severe retribution if their identities were known.

"The white nationalist gathering on Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc land this morning was hateful and meant to intimidate. It has no place in British Columbia," said Lorne Doerkson, interim leader of the B.C. Conservative Party, in a post to social media.
He added that the "B.C. Conservatives condemn it completely."

items: Anti-Indigenous racism increasing around Powell River, say Tla'amin Nation citizens

blocks.text: CentreBC Leader Elenore Sturko, in a post on social media, called the gathering "abhorrent."

"Hate and discrimination of any kind are unwelcome in British Columbia and on behalf of all members of Centre BC, I condemn this behaviour and stand in solidarity with the Tkʼemlúps First Nation," she said.
Plans for the nation's events for Truth and Reconciliation Day on Sept. 30, Casimir said, will go ahead.
"We will not be intimidated," said Casimir.
"This is not going to deter us from gathering, reflecting, or honouring our survivors and the children who returned home," she said.
But this incident, Casimir said, is an example of a broader problem.
"Everyone should always be concerned because there's so much racism and discrimination out there."
She said Tk'emlúps te Secwépemc will keep its community members informed if there are further safety concerns.
CBC News reached out to Second Sons Canada but did not hear back before publication.
A national 24-hour Indian Residential School Crisis Line is available at 1-866-925-4419 for emotional and crisis referral services for survivors and those affected.
Mental health counselling and crisis support are also available 24 hours a day, seven days a week through the Hope for Wellness hotline at 1-855-242-3310 or by online chat.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Arden McLeod, from Vancouver, is an associate producer with CBC News. He has a passion for community storytelling, local news, and reflecting the values of B.C. He graduated from the British Columbia Institute of Technology's broadcast and online journalism program. You can reach him at Arden.McLeod@cbc.ca.

France’s far-right National Rally (RN) party and its…

blocks.text: France’s far-right National Rally (RN) party and its allies have secured a record 14 seats in the rightwing-dominated Senate in elections, effectively quadrupling its number in the 348-seat chamber just months before a presidential poll.
RN presidential candidate Marine Le Pen called the results an “historic victory” after they were announced on Sunday. “The results ‌have exceeded our expectations,” she said.
It was the first time the ⁠party had cleared the 10-seat threshold to be able to form a Senate caucus.
Local elected officials vote for new senators for half the upper chamber every three years, each to serve a six-year term.
The far-right party entered the Senate for the first time with two seats in 2014, when it was known as the National Front, and won three seats in 2023.
Le Pen is considering her best chance yet at power in elections scheduled for a first round in April next year when the centrist president, Emmanuel Macron, steps down.
“This is a historic victory, and a major milestone with the formation for the first time of a group in the Senate,” she said on X.
Nine RN senators were elected on Sunday, according to an AFP tally of results, on top of the three who won seats in 2023.
A further two were elected from RN ally Eric Ciotti’s Union of the Right for the Republic (UDR) party.
RN’s president, Jordan Bardella, said the party’s senators would form a group with UDR allies.

blocks.caption: RN president Jordan Bardella (C) poses with supporters in La Seyne-sur-Mer, southern France, on Sunday as the far right won a record 14 seats in Senate elections. Photograph: Thibaud Moritz/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Ciotti quit the rightwing Republicans (LR) party in 2024 after calling for an alliance with the far right.
The upper chamber’s LR president of more than a decade, Gerard Larcher, 77, is expected to be re-elected next week.
The right, centre and leftwing Socialists looked set to remain the three major forces in the upper house, according to initial results.
The hard-left France Unbowed party won a seat for the first time.
Le Pen’s anti-immigration party emerged as the single largest party in the lower-house National Assembly after Macron called snap polls in 2024, although it fell well short of a majority.
With Reuters

articles.title: Gracioso was demoted, suspended at least thrice before dismissal, NAPOLCOM records show
articles.summary: The National Police Commission suspended former policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr thrice before dismissing him from service on September 15, 2026, official records show.

blocks.text: The National Police Commission suspended former policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr thrice before dismissing him from service on September 15, 2026, official records show.

Gracioso, who claimed to have worked as a security aide for former House Speaker Lord Allan Velasco, said he delivered cash and other gifts to Vice President Sara Duterte, former President Rodrigo Duterte, and Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo "Pulong" Duterte.
The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is investigating Gracioso’s claims.
According to NAPOLCOM records obtained by GMA News, Philippine National Police chief Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr ordered the dismissal of Gracioso due to “three counts of less grave misconduct.”
The order was dated September 15, 2026, one day after he submitted his official sworn and subscribed affidavit to the NBI on September 14.
The dismissal, effective September 11, also ordered the penalties of cancellation of eligibility, forfeiture of retirement benefits, and disqualification for re-employment in government service.
GMA News also obtained Gracioso’s service record that shows he had three suspensions prior to his dismissal.
Gracioso was suspended on March 1-11, 2024, October 21-December 18, 2025, and February 1-July 31, 2026.
The order for his suspension on October 20, 2025 said Gracioso was suspended for 59 days due to grave threat.
Along with this suspension order in 2025, the NAPOLCOM also demoted Gracioso from police corporal to patrolman, due to two counts of grave misconduct and for conduct unbecoming of a police officer.
The service record also indicated he was detained twice on November 15-21, 2024 and December 11-January 9, 2025.

The NBI gave GMA News a copy of Gracioso’s affidavit where he detailed alleged deliveries of suitcases containing millions of cash to Vice President Sara Duterte, former President Rodrigo Duterte, and Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo Duterte.
Vice President Sara Duterte however on Saturday said she does not know Gracioso, and she did not receive any money from him.
"Mga kababayan, I do not know Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., nor have I ever received any money from him," Duterte said in a statement.
"My lawyers are awaiting an official copy of the Gracioso affidavit from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) so they can begin working on the cases to be filed against him," she added.
"Once we are done dismantling the lies contained in his testimony, it will end up in the trash bin—just like the one from Ramil Madriaga," Duterte said.
The vice president said Gracioso's allegation is "another media stunt," adding that the Marcos administration is bent on bringing her down.
Velasco’s camp on Saturday said the allegations against him had “no basis.”

"The former Speaker of the House's record of service in the government is untainted with corruption and his wife's benevolence is widely known, leaving no basis for the illegal allegations now being suggested," said Velasco's spokesperson Atty. Rowell Ilagan in a statement.

"The 'one-size-fits-all' narration by this individual seems to be designed and fabricated to attack as many targets as it can while being inconsistent with verifiable events, that is, the COVID-19 pandemic, Atty. Velasco's period of service as speaker, other details, and even basic common sense," he added.
Former chief presidential legal counsel Salvador Panelo said on Sunday that Gracioso’s claims is a “fabricated story” to oust and disqualify Vice President Sara Duterte in the 2028 elections.
“The Gracioso concoction is obviously another fabricated story, pure and simple black propaganda, just like the Madriaga affidavit,” Panelo said in a statement.

“The brains behind the ouster and disqualification of VP Sara in the 2028 presidential elections will stop at nothing in order to succeed in their devious plan of obliterating her from the political landscape and from the face of the earth,” he added.
GMA News has sought comments through phone calls and messages to Paolo Duterte since Thursday, but he has yet to give any.

House prosecution panel spokesperson Representative Zia Adiong of Lanao del Sur meanwhile on Saturday said that claims that Sara Duterte received suitcases containing billions of pesos “have to be taken seriously.” —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Mideast oil exports rebound in September as Saudi Arabia boosts shipments
articles.summary: The rebound follows a recovery in exports via the Strait of Hormuz, which are set to hit about 7.4 million bpd this month, as Saudi Arabia diverts oil exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu following…

blocks.text: INCREASE. Another round of fuel price hikes takes effect in Manila, on April 7, 2026.
Rappler

The rebound follows a recovery in exports via the Strait of Hormuz, which are set to hit about 7.4 million bpd this month, as Saudi Arabia diverts oil exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu following attacks that damaged its East-West pipeline

SINGAPORE – Crude oil exports from key Middle East producers rebounded in September to 12.8 million barrels per day, the highest since the US-Israeli war with Iran started in February, data from Kpler showed on Monday, September 28, as Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates boosted exports.

The rebound came following a recovery in exports via the Strait of Hormuz, which were set to hit about 7.4 million bpd this month, as Saudi Arabia diverted oil exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu following attacks that damaged its East-West pipeline, the preliminary data showed.

blocks.caption: Allies unite behind Saudi Arabia as Houthis step up attacks

blocks.text: While exports from the region – which includes Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Iraq, Oman, Qatar, Kuwait and Iran – have rebounded, they were still about 6 million bpd down from 18.8 million bpd in February, according to Kpler.
The region’s top exporter, Saudi Arabia, was on track to ship about 5.4 million bpd this month, rebounding from 2.446 million bpd in August, the data showed.

September shipments from the Ras Tanura port in the Gulf jumped to about 3.6 million bpd, from 929,000 bpd in August, but still lower than the 6.411 million bpd recorded in February, according to the data.
A total of 19 very large crude carriers, carrying 2 million barrels of Saudi oil each, exited the Strait of Hormuz last week, Kpler data showed.
The figures exclude any vessels that might have crossed the strait with their Automatic Identification System transponders turned off to avoid detection.

Before the Iran war started on February 28, the strait typically handled about 125 large commercial vessels per day, including tankers, gas carriers, bulkers and container vessels, accounting for some 20% of the world’s daily crude oil and liquefied natural gas supply. – Rappler.com
